answer: A seat exists only while a distinct physical chip vouches for it. Each chip carries a pearl, an attestation key fused into its secure element that never leaves the silicon. The garden, a shared registry, maps every pearl to one identity and rejects a second binding. Each epoch the chip signs the beacon plus a monotonic counter, extending the seat's thread; a repeated or rolled-back count exposes a cloned enclave. Every fake must buy its own attested board, about $40, sunk even if never flagged: 500 fakes mean $20,000 of hardware.
